AP behavior:
After STA G3, the AP retains the old session state and has an SA Query in progress. As a result, it correctly rejects the STA Association Request with status 30 (comeback). The STA waits for the comeback interval and then retries the association. At this point, since the interval has elapsed, the AP should accept the request. Instead, the AP sends a Deauthentication frame with reason code 6 (CLASS2_FRAME_FROM_NONAUTH_STA), which is non-compliant behavior.

Why the reconnect fails:
The driver correctly treats reason code 6 as recoverable and initiates a fresh connection attempt. However, a race condition in the driver can cause this retry to fail, leading to “No suitable network found” / “No enabled networks,” and don't try to do actual connection.
In addition, when we retrigger a connection, we are not preserving the connect token, so even if we'll be able to connect the driver will eventually fail. Fix both issues.

We noticed that when another part of our system, the scan module, asked the DSM for permission to use that data, the DSM attempted to complete the request but was interrupted by entering a low-power mode. This interruption prevented the process from finishing properly, lowering the LTR and allowing the machine to enter its own low-power state. We've updated the system so that the DSM can continue to manage these requests even if it goes into low-power mode, which should resolve the problem.

[BUGFIX]  Coex: Fix Sync2Bt Timer Loss Sync

(-) Bug:
     Sync2Bt Timer is keep expired since in the past and prevent any LMAC other activity.

(-) Bug Description:
    Sync2BT Timer is use sync2BtRise-Timestamp in order to set the next timer expiration..
    But when the Sync2BtRise-Timestamp is in the past and not advanced for a long time
    it result with continues Sync2BtTimer expired and actually prevent any LMAC other activity

(-) Bug Scenario:
     Sync2Bt is enabled & working on timer, WiFi is on LB
     During that, WiFi is triggered Calbrations on HB which result with Phy LB Deactivate
     and Aux Phy Activate on HB. Following that on FullCoexOff we set Sync2BT Disable reason = SYNC_2_BT_BT_PROTOCOL_DIS
     Status: Sync2Bt is enabled from BT Side but since we are on HB now the Disable reason should allow all Tx but the tracking should continue.

    Then following mailbox we get to sync2BtEngineStatusUpdate() with sync2BT enabled status.
    but on _sync2BtEngineUpdatePtaInterrupts() since we ask for sync2BtEngineIsSync2BtAllowed() we disable the sync2Bt kick filter
    while the Sync2Bt machnisem (timer) is stiil working.

Bug Solution :
  (-) Remove the dependency of sync2BtEngineIsSync2BtAllowed on _sync2BtEngineUpdatePtaInterrupts.
       Following that  as long as Sync2BT is enabled the Sync2BT mechanism will keep working even when we enter to HB Phy.
       Only in case Sync2BT is disabled (by BT MBX or by CI change) the Sync2BT mechanism will disabled.
       Note - When Sync2BT mechanism is working but Phy is on Non LB (Aux\Calib) the Tx will allowed and not defered.

When we receive data, the rate of ack/BA calculation is based on rate from RX packet
on of the parameters in the rate is antenna selection

the calculation of antenna selection in ack is based on RSSI of RX packet

In CCK there is a bug, that we first make decision of what antenna to use and only after that read rssi of rx packet from registers

In this case the RSSI in the decision is 0 for both antennas and in this case (when rssi is equal for both antennas) our algorithm takes antenna B always (not shared antenna with BT).

So the solution is to read rssi values of rx in right place, and only then make decision what antenna to use

Since PC migration doesn't call FreeLibrary for MurocApi DLL, the destructor that suppose to close PIE and PipeClient threads is not called. It's an incorrect behavior by the PC migration.
Up until 22.220, PIE and PipeClient used CreateThread API to open those threads, threads that are created using this API are closed (not gracefully) when the process is closed.
In 22.230, CreateThread API was replaced with std::async API, threads that are created by std::async must be closed before closing the process, otherwise the process will keep running.
In order to mitigate such an incorrect behavior, we changed std::async back to CreateThread.

Flush PCI pipe before completing the PNP_SET_POWER task.
Fix for a race that was found on weak CPU/PCI, where
driver is writing into a CSR, however, the actual right occurs
after we complete the PNP_SET_POWER task.
This causes WHEA unrecoverable error and leading to BSOD 0x124.
Due to weak CPU, or might be a combination with multiple
PCI bridges on this platform, the actual write is not instant.

For some reason, issue was not seen on Win10, while stated appearing
on Win11 - might be different PCI error handling logic.

Deeper analysis: it was seen using PCI analyzer that after driver
is completing the PNP_SET_POWER task, OS puts the PCI in low power mode,
and no further transactions are allowed. However, then we see a memory
write TLP - our CSR write, which was obviously initiated before.

As a WA, need to “flush” the PCI, by reading from the last written CSR
before competing the task. This should ensure that all previous
transactions have completed and it is safe to put PCI into sleep.

[BUGFIX] mvm: don't account for the losing time of the wrong link

    When we want to look for a hole for an event, and our event is placed
    after event B, we want to make sure that we leave room for the link that
    runs event B to loose the medium properly before we run our event.
    In case of GO / BSS in SCM, we can have the following scenario:

    GO's beacon saver ends at 100
    BSS'es TBTT ends at 50

    This means that we could place an event at 101 since the losing time of
    the GO is 0, but we don't since we want to leave enough time for the
    losing for the client.

    This wouldn't be a big problem if we didn't have to re-allocate events.
    I saw in USIM the following problem:

    1) time is now 50
    2) GO / BSS in SCM, beacon of the GO is at 150, beacon of the BSS at 100
    3) Fragmented scan allocates events (50 ms long)
    4) We place one time NOA for a fragment of the scan at time 180, after
       the next beacon of the GO (because of the beacon saver)
       Note that this overrides the BSS's TBTT which is fine.
    5) the beacon saver event of the GO ends at 180 to give room for the
       scan event
    6) time passes by, we are at 100
    7) TBTT of the BSS runs and we remove the occurrence after beacon Rx
    8) Refresh
    9) we place again the the scan's fragment, but this time we place it at
       180 + BSS's losing time.
    <=== This is the bug ===>

    We just moved the fragmented scan's event, but we had a NOA that was
    placed exactly for that specific event and now the fragmented scan's
    event is unfortunate because of the beacon saver of the GO.

    We could have placed the fragmented scan's event again at 180 because
    the client already knows it needs to have left the channel by 180. But
    because we take into account the losing time of the BSS after an event
    that belongs to the GO, we delay the scan event by 4ms and it misses the
    window created by the GO's NOA.

    Fix this by looking at the losing time of the link of the specific event
    that precedes the hole, and do not consider all the events in the
    binding.

Fixed deadlock between RouterDLL and PIE IHV.

Those threads are opened by a "KeepAlive" timer which runs a function every second to check if the connection to RPC is still valid.
The connection to RPC check is done by running an API that is sent to the RPC server, if the API fails, it returns an error.
When the Wlanext.exe process is in "pending" state, the RPC server doesn't respond to the RPC call which blocks the call forever (Bug in MSRPC).
Since the call is blocked, and the timer is still running, every second another thread is being stuck, and this is why there are so many threads.
To solve this, I put a boolean that signals if there is already a running thread, if there is already a running thread, the function will exit without doing anything.

PIE is using an asynchronous method in order to send a bind event, in this case there was a racing condition between that method and the FreeLibrary call:
1) Asynchronous method is called.
2) Router frees the PIE IHV module while the method is still working.
3) The asynchronous method is still working while the main thread of the DLL that host that method is closed.
4) This causes Wlanext.exe process to remain open.
5) On driver enable, a new Wlanext.exe process is created.
6) Since there are 2 running Wlanext.exe processes, this means that the RPC server is still working in the old process which prevents creating a new RPC server connection in the new process.
7) PIE service tries to connect to the RPC server which is stuck on the old process, which makes the service to also be stuck.

the LOST_OWNERSHIP flow, which would call the command callbacks and complete the

Debug has shown the INA controllers become stuck in illegal state, in which there can be no preamble detections until the RX is reset. This happens when packets are received in high input power and the receiver is reset while such packet is still on air.

We traced the cause to a combination of INA HW bug and a long-existing FW workaround:

There’s a config register called CCK_PURE_11B which disables the OFDM preamble detector. It was originally intended to be used with APs that support CCK only without OFDM. Since it was considered an esoteric feature it was not thoroughly validated.
Due to HW bug, if CCK_PURE_11B=1 and there’s high incoming power which leads to AGC Fast Step, it’s possible for the preamble detection module to remain turned off when it’s supposed to turn on. Whether that happens depends on relative phase between 2 clock signals when entering a specific state of the controller FSM. Having the preamble detector turned off instead of on prevents detection, and it also prevent restoring the gain to max since the controller waits for the detector to indicate that preamble wasn’t found. It’s only possible to exist this state by toggling rx_en, or if CCK detection is not required as in HB.

Description: In master, the FW (Data Path) controls the key table, but in core43 (Thunder,
our case) the Driver controls it, except for D3 then the FW (WoWlan and DP) controls it.
Before the security refactoring driver sent add_sta_key command with delete key flag for every key on disconnection flow.
During the refactoring, FW requested not to send add_sta_key command with delete flag on disconnection and FW will clean the sta key when removing the station (there is a special handle for this request on driver code). Driver will only clean internally.
FW don't delete the key in its table (BUG!)  when the driver do delete it in his parallel table keys,
leading to scenario in which after more than 15 rekeys in D0 and eventually rekey in D3, FW can't find empty key index although there are free indexes.
According to Lotem Bar-yaakov, the issue is not trivial to solve on FW side, we deliver a fix on driver:
1. send delete FW command in case of release peer
2. send delete FW command with the Old key index in case of adding new key in re-key flow.

Debug has shown the INA controllers become stuck in illegal state, in which there can be no preamble detections until the RX is reset. This happens when packets are received in high input power and the receiver is reset while such packet is still on air.

We traced the cause to a combination of INA HW bug and a long-existing FW workaround:

There’s a config register called CCK_PURE_11B which disables the OFDM preamble detector. It was originally intended to be used with APs that support CCK only without OFDM. Since it was considered an esoteric feature it was not thoroughly validated.
Due to HW bug, if CCK_PURE_11B=1 and there’s high incoming power which leads to AGC Fast Step, it’s possible for the preamble detection module to remain turned off when it’s supposed to turn on. Whether that happens depends on relative phase between 2 clock signals when entering a specific state of the controller FSM. Having the preamble detector turned off instead of on prevents detection, and it also prevent restoring the gain to max since the controller waits for the detector to indicate that preamble wasn’t found. It’s only possible to exist this state by toggling rx_en, or if CCK detection is not required as in HB.

[BUGFIX] Fix rare race between remove peer and tx scheduler assign

Description: There is a rare race but still possible due to module design and implementation.
1. Core 0: Got a packet for peer/tid (0,0). This is the only packet for the queue
2. Core 0: Packet pass classification and processing. Packet on ready state AND scheduler was not triggered yet
3. Core 1: Remove peer flow triggered
4. Core 1: Flush flow doesn't send command to FW (no scheduled packets) and return the packet sync.
5. Core 1: Remove peer flow release peer schedulers (nothing to do as no scheduler was assign)
6. Core 1: Remove peer completed
7. Core 0: Continue the flow calling txResourcesMgrAssignTxScheduler regardless if there are (or not) packets and if peer still exists.

Trying to allocated a scheduler for a non-exist peer will cause unexpected behavior -> assert or BSOD.

The fix:
Check if peer still exist without calling txResourcesMgrAssignTxScheduler

This issue only occurs on HE connection due to HTC support bit in HE MAC capabilities.
Galaxy S10 decides to turn on the 'Order Flag' bit in the DHCP frame control flags due to this bit.
This bit means that the MAC header has 4 additional bytes of HT Control (HTC).
The LLC comes right after the MAC header in the packet.
The OS complains that the LLC is invalid, even tho in pass/fail cases the LLC is the same.
If we remove the additional 4 bytes of HTC the connection succeeds.

Therefore this seems to be like an OS issue which is not taking the extra 4 bytes into consideration, thus dropping the DHCP request and not sending a DHCP reply for the driver to send.

As a temporal fix, disable the HTC supported bit in HE MAC capabilities for softAP/GO.

Wowlan feature is based on preventing WLAN MAC Reset during S3 and S4 – keeping the mac alive while the Host in S3/S4 therefore the mac can receive the magic packets and wake the host.
The WLAN reset prevented by using a control signal called “Persistence”. 
Persistence == (Device in D3 ) & (PME_EN) == Power Management  Control / Status Register (PCIe CFG space) bits [1:0] (PowerState)  & bits [8]  (PME_ENABLE)
The bug in WLAN device is  that : Power Management  Control / Status Register (PCIe CFG space) bits [1:0] (PowerState)  was reset during entry to L2 , due to race condition which cause the internal LTSSSM machine to move into Detect State 
Instead of staying in L2 State.
Once the LTSSM moved to Detect the  power state changed to D0 and Persistence was cleared. 

The WA provided is : before going to D3 the WLAN FW receive an indication for the Driver that host is going to D3. In addition to other process the FW “force the persistence “ to ignore the D3 conditionץ
This keeps the MAC from getting the RESET .

The Bug was fix in later silicones after WsP/8265 (fixed over ThP/9260 and newer products).

Due to historic HW issue on BT (BT only catch the interrupt rising edge so need to toggle it after writing data to MBX in order BT will get interrupt to our MBX.), there is WA for handling this issue that is done by using shrMbx infra : 

o Read Status register of WIFI2BT. ---------->[ int1RegVal = (shrMbxHalIntrRead(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT) ] 
o Clear Status register of WIFI2BT. ----------> [ shrMbxHalIntrClearBits(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, MBX_REG_DEFAULT_BITMASK) ] 
o Write to Cause register what we read & the new type we send now (DBGC MSG) --> [ shrMbxHalIntrWrite(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, (g_typesToSend | int1RegVal) << 8) ]. 

This write will set interrupt status bit and triggers interrupt rising edge for BT. 

This above handling is done by using shrMbx Infra which is wrong due the READ & CLEAR function always approach BT2WIFI registers (offset from CNVI_AUX_MBX_MASTER_0_TO_1_STATUS) instead of WF2BT. 

In bug WIFI-16623 this issue caused us to miss mbox rcv messages on power up flow since on power up flow we send DBGC message before handling the rcv messages and because of the bug we clear the interrupt bit of BT2WF instead of WF2BT. 

In this scenario we got mbox message of TYPE2 and we try to send mbox message of type7. Before sending it we read the interrupt status register of BT2WF (instead of WF2BT) and we get bit2 set since we got mbox TYPE2 from BT. Then when we write to WF2BT status register we add the value we read (bit2) so BT gets interrupt of message TYPE2 although we didn't intend to send such message, and it reads data reg7 which contains garbage and ATS bit it set there.

When loading FW the, driver triggers WD on FW load.
In case FW load WD expired, the NIC SM enters ERROR state, before resetting FW it waits for all DPCs to complete (inside the NIC SM lock)
In case the FW load complete DPC is handled on a different core, it will try to take the NIC SM lock in order to indicate the NIC load complete event, this causes a deadlock between the thread that has the SM lock waiting for the DPC to complete and the DPC thread that is waiting for the SM lock.

Fix was to split the NIC SM reset event to 2 steps. Step one waits for all DPCs to complete inside a job (async)
This will avoid the wait for DPC to wait while taking the NIC SM lock.
Once wait for DPC is over, NIC ever RESET_STEP_2 will be triggered to continue FW reset

Drain runs in a job and after calling internal TX CBs.
When complete is called prior to calling internal TX CBs, peer can be removed by GO, before drain complete is called.
This can happen when GO sent DEAUTH frame to peer and drain started (in case of shared Q).
TX complete will come and will call drain complete, which will remove peer from DP DB and destroy the GO client's SM.
Later on, this frame will be forwarded to GO which will try to dispatch it into the SM which was destroyed earlier.

The fix:
1. Always call drain complete after calling internal TX CBs
2. Make sure that drain complete starts new JOB in order to break the stack
and make sure that jib runs last

When loading FW the, driver triggers WD on FW load. 
In case FW load WD expired, the NIC SM enters ERROR state, before resetting FW it waits for all DPCs to complete (inside the NIC SM lock) 
In case the FW load complete DPC is handled on a different core, it will try to take the NIC SM lock in order to indicate the NIC load complete event, this causes a deadlock between the thread that has the SM lock waiting for the DPC to complete and the DPC thread that is waiting for the SM lock. 

Fix was to split the NIC SM reset event to 2 steps. Step one waits for all DPCs to complete inside a job (async) 
This will avoid the wait for DPC to wait while taking the NIC SM lock. 
Once wait for DPC is over, NIC ever RESET_STEP_2 will be triggered to continue FW reset

TFD Q tail invalidation protection.
Due to wrong calculation of TFD->count, we can enter into an infinite loops while dispatching.
In case of fake TX response for single packets, prvTfdQueueInvalidateTail is called and it will (finally, after many TXs) decrement TFD->count below zero (or to a large UINT32).
When reset comes, DP aborts all committed packets (txTidQueueAbortCommitedPackets) and will fetch queue->count (numOfPendingEntrys).
Trying to dispatch this huge number will result in commutative DPC WD BSOD (0x133_1).

The fix:
1. to guard TFD->count. add additional checkers (prvTfdQueueInvalidateTail)
2. single TX complete (prvTfdQueueSendComplete) check also command response sequence number (TFD index) and make sure it is equal to TFD->tail driver has

WDI: max supported SGLs (per NBL), use 19 instead of 8
Current capability to WDI is to support up to 8 SGLs per NBL.
This value is hardcoded, since 'normal' NBLs should not have more than this value.
However, in case of LSO, we can exceed it, since we support up to 32 KB LSO size, where each SGL is limited to page size (4 KB). 
In such case, where NBL has more than 8 SGLs, WDI will drop it. (it will try to 'fix' it, and might fail).

The fix for CC30 is to enlarge this value to 19 (MAX_TBs - 1). The maximal NBL which we can transmit (in case we do not copy it) can contain 19 SGLs.
This is a HW limitation (ThP and below) for the TX command. TBs array has 20 entries.

The fix for main will have different logic: driver will not limit this value and will be support up to 0xFFFF (infinity).
In case we are getting NBL with more than MAX_TBs - 1 SGLs, driver will drop it (or copy). In such way, the drop will be monitored and visible.

Peer is accepting connection and making role switch.
Role switch is passing good however, Intel DUT (Peripheral now) is
sending LMP_Set_AFH following the role switch.

The root cause for this issue is a race between the processing of
RS message and lmp-accepted-for-host-conn-request-packet.

RS and LMP don't pass the same flow:
Role switch related messages:	BC-> LC-> LLC-> LM
PDU packet reception:		BC-> LC-> LM

Since PDU packet reception has fewer steps than RS, LM may move to the
new role (slave role) too late.
When lmp-accepted-for-host-conn-request-packet is received at LM,
LM layer can still be in the old role (master)
i.e., LM is in old role, and LC is in the new role.

As a fix, the setup complete process is postponed till RS message is

Problem statement: As part of system preparation using sysprep.exe and generalization in Windows Audit mode, the Bluetooth driver resulted in YB.

Background: The Intel Tile Node is a raw PDO that exposes interface for Tile application to send request to Driver though IO CTL interface. The raw PDO will appear as hidden device in Device manager under Other devices section without any device properties. OEMs raised a concern about the new node also requested to populate device properties for this node to adopt in the OEM Automation / testing. As part of adding the Device Properties for Tile Node, the Intel Tile Node device is made as child device for Bluetooth driver node to inherit all the properties of Parent. To achieve this, ibtusb.inf is modified to represent Tile Node as Null Device and child of Intel Bluetooth Driver.

Analysis: As part of Driver installation using MSI, the package will install all the drivers that are included in it . This is a PNP installation requirement to support Plug and Play of devices. The MSI will install all the driver including CcP and HrP which contains the Tile Node INF entries though the platform having TyP connected. The Driver will included the firmware for respective SKUs only. After Installation in audit mode and then performing Generalization, It is observed that Windows OS is loading different SKU driver Binary ( in this case it is CCP) where the TyP firmware will not be present. Due to this, the driver will result in Yellow Bang. This has been confirmed form the driver logs.

This has been narrowed down further by uninstalling the CcP and HrP SKU drivers manually after installation and then performing the Generalization in audit mode. In this case, the Windows OS is loading the driver Binary for the respective SKUs.
Few more points:
- Bluetooth Driver name (ibtusb.sys) and INF(ibtusb.inf) is same for all SKUs .
- The Intel Tile Node INF Entries are present only in HrP and CcP. These drivers are installed as part of MSI package and which binds the Tile node with ibtusb.sys/ibtusb.inf ( Additional clarification required here from MSFT )
- The issue is narrowed down only. However, the root cause of the issue still need to be investigated based on feedback from MSFT. We have Open sighting with MSFT PnP team on this (https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16012307683 ).

Test Coverage: As part of Test coverage, all the testing including the installation is performed in Normal windows mode. Switching between Normal OS to Audit mode and then Generalization is not covered. This is the process followed in Factories for imaging the platforms. This is the gap identified and is required to add testing coverage in Install domain areas.

The delay function MBX_SEMAPHORE_RETRY_DELAY_uSEC(4); is implemented based on the slot and bit counter value. These registers are not accessible when active park is enabled. When active park is enabled, these registers always give zero value and the delay loop will enter into infinite loop and it will trigger watchdog timeout exception. To fix this issue, replaced the delay function MBX_SEMAPHORE_RETRY_DELAY_uSEC(4); with simple "for" loop delay which eliminates dependency on special registers for the purpose of introducing delay.

When there is a quick transition from USB suspend to resume from host, wakeup interrupt may be already set while processing suspend. In addition on CNVi designs, at the end of suspend processing during partial power down entry, suspend_n signal is asserted, This signal goes as input signal to U2U bridge. In such corner case condition, wakeup may be triggered before programming PPD setting or after programming the PPD setting. If
wakeup is detected before programming PPD setting, FW don't allow PPD entry. If PPD entry setting is done by the FW,  this fix ensures the worst case propagation delay required for synchronizer logic (4 * 32KHz clock cycles period) before PPD exit setting is programmed. This ensures suspend_n de-assertion is properly propagated (through synchronizer logic) to U2U bridge and UTMI clock switches are stabilized.

FW is designed to start guard timer when LC while programs BC job. This guard timer is to detect if job could not begin, and initiate recovery procedure and re-invoke pre-processor.
In case of this issue, job was started correctly, and LC_WAKEUP_MSG was posted by BC layer, and lc_preProcessor was stared, but before stopping guard timer, AFH channel classification/aging algorithm is invoked which is taking 700+ uS.
In the meantime, guard timer expired and as part of recovery mechanism, it cancels current and next job, which is incorrect.
On the other hand, BC layer (unaware of guard timer expiry) continues with current ongoing job. This sometimes results FATAL exceptions or connection timeouts depending on BC state when guard timer ISR was invoked.

Fix:
On receiving LC_WAKEUP_MSG, lc_preProcessor should first stop guard timer and then run the AFH channel/classification/aging algorithm

In a LE-Link, as Master the Link State is updated to LC_LE_LINKSTATE_PHY_UPDATE_PENDING even before transmitting the PHY_UPDATE_IND PDU (i.e. when the PDU is queued).
If the PHY_UPDATE_IND PDU transmission gets delayed because of other items in the transmission queue or because of NACK, then there is a chance that the linkstate will be updated back to ACTIVE (as part of lc_LECollectRequest), since the PHY Update Instant is not filled in the PDU untill the PDU is picked for transmission.
And when the PDU is actually picked for transmission, the linkstate is no more PHY_UPDATE_PENDING, it is ACTIVE and this results in Instant not filled in the PDU, which can cause the remote device to terminate connection upon reception of this PDU and result in Connection Loss.

WHQL failures reported in this Issue are due to FW watchdog exceptions. One of the LE Scan transaction has corrupted endTransaction native slot programmed, which caused all subsequent jobs to be incorrectly programmed. When this happens, LC scheduler will not be able program BC layer and start a job, and just keep running LC Preprocessor forever until WD exception occurs.

LE scans are of 37ms window size. If controller gets a sync within this window, then LC scheduler will try to program another LE Scan window for the time remaining in the 37ms window.
It looks like the issue (incorrect end native slot) happens while programming the second LE scan window. when very little scan window is left for the second scan transaction

Fix:
As we know that the endTransaction native slot is getting corrupted, a check is added if the duration of the Current Job is greater than 100ms then the Job is cancelled and preprocessor is called which will schedule the next job based on the current native slot instead of the corrupted endTransaction native slot.

The issue happens when an USB ISR for SCO happens after SCO connection has been terminated. 

The exact issue is because of current logic where 0 bytes are read form Ring Buffer if SCO connections has been terminated and there are no active SCO connections. The exit condition for loop causing watchdog is that required number of bytes are read form ring buffer. After checking that ring buffer has this many required bytes, controller does a check inside loop if a SCO connection is active or not. If not it will read 0 bytes from RING BUFFER. This causes required bytes to stay constant and leads to controller stuck in a loop.

The Fix is to break loop in above condition.

Due to historic HW issue on BT (BT only catch the interrupt rising edge so need to toggle it after writing data to MBX in order BT will get interrupt to our MBX.),  there is WA for handling this issue that is done by using shrMbx infra :

o Read Status register of WIFI2BT. ---------->[ int1RegVal = (shrMbxHalIntrRead(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT) ] 
o Clear Status register of WIFI2BT. ----------> [ shrMbxHalIntrClearBits(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, MBX_REG_DEFAULT_BITMASK) ] 
o Write to Cause register what we read & the new type we send now (DBGC MSG) --> [ shrMbxHalIntrWrite(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, (g_typesToSend | int1RegVal) << 8) ].

This write will set interrupt status bit and triggers interrupt rising edge for BT.

This above handling is done by using shrMbx Infra which is wrong due the READ & CLEAR function always approach BT2WIFI registers (offset from CNVI_AUX_MBX_MASTER_0_TO_1_STATUS) instead of WF2BT.

In bug WIFI-16623 this issue caused us to miss mbox rcv messages on power up flow since on power up flow we send DBGC message before handling the rcv messages and because of the bug we clear the interrupt bit of BT2WF instead of WF2BT.

In this scenario we got mbox message of TYPE2 and we try to send mbox message of type7. Before sending it we read the interrupt status register of BT2WF (instead of WF2BT) and we get bit2 set since we got mbox TYPE2 from BT. Then when we write to WF2BT status register we add the value we read (bit2) so BT gets interrupt of message TYPE2 although we didn't intend to send such message, and it reads data reg7 which contains garbage and ATS bit it set there.

4. Reconnection procedure is started.

After wake up, Lullaby test was either reusing existing handle to audio device or was fast enough to open audio device before re-connection happened. In turn, Lullaby2 test was failing during/after re-connection happened (somewhere between steps 3 and 5).

Suspend/Resume handling was like this:
1. Get notification from system about transition to Sx state.
2. Execute "Disconnection Process"
3. Get notification from system about Bluetooth is about to shutdown
4. Get notification from system about wake up
5. Wait for audio device wake up
6. Initiate reconnection

I.e., we are initiating execution of "Disconnection Process" as soon as we got notificaton about transition to Sx state.

since we are on ADV channel and share a common access code, it is possible for us to sync on a spurious ADV packet while we are actually expecting a Scan response.
